title: The interpretation of computational model parameters depends on the context
description: 291 participants aged 8 to 30 completed three reinforcement-learning tasks in one session; RL models were fitted to each task, and the paper tests whether the parameters (noise/exploration, positive and negative learning rates, forgetting) generalise between tasks (absolute values, rank order, age trajectories, cross-task prediction, comparison with a generalisability ceiling) and whether they are interpretable (principal components, cross-validated ridge regression). Some parameters generalised partly, only between sufficiently similar tasks; others did not.
